approved.title: KENYA JUNIOR SECONDARY SCHOOL SCHEME OF WORK
approved.subtitle: GRADE 7 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS (CAS) - TERM 3
approved.subject: CAS

rows: Subject
Creative Arts and Sports (CAS)
Grade Level
Grade 7
Term
Term 3
Duration
14 Weeks
Curriculum Framework
KICD Competency-Based Curriculum (CBC)
Core Competencies
Communication and Collaboration, Critical Thinking and Problem Solving, Creativity and Imagination, Digital Literacy, Self-efficacy
Values
Respect, Responsibility, Unity, Integrity, Patriotism, Social Justice
Assessment Modes
Practical Demonstration, Observation Rubrics, Portfolio Evaluation, Oral Questioning, Peer/Self-Assessment, Written Tests
Week 1
Performing Arts
Wind Instruments (Descant Recorder)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Identify fingering techniques for notes C, D, E, and F on a descant recorder; b) Play simple melodic patterns using proper breath control; c) Appreciate playing wind instruments in harmony.
How does proper breath control affect tone quality on a descant recorder?
Learners practice holding the recorder with correct posture, finger placement for notes C, D, E, F, and play basic melodic exercises individually and in groups.
Descant recorders, fingering charts, audio samples, music exercise books.
Practical demonstration, Observation checklist, Oral questioning
Week 2
Performing Arts
Melody and Rhythm Creation

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Compose a 4-bar rhythmic pattern using crotchets and quavers; b) Perform the composed rhythm using body percussion; c) Display confidence during rhythmic performances.
How can body percussion enhance rhythmic performances?
Learners collaborate in groups to write 4-bar rhythms on rhythmic charts, tap/clap the rhythms, and present body percussion routines to the class.
Rhythm charts, percussion instruments (drums, shakers), manuscript papers.
Portfolio assessment, Group performance, Peer evaluation
Week 3
Visual Arts
Sculpture and Modelling (3D Art)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Prepare clay material suitable for modeling; b) Model a three-dimensional human figure showing basic proportion; c) Value neatness and safety when handling clay tools.
Why is proportion important in three-dimensional sculpture?
Learners knead clay to remove air bubbles, construct basic torso and limb structures, join parts using slip, and shape a human figure in motion.
Clay, water, clay modeling tools, modeling boards, sample sculptures.
Portfolio (artifacts), Practical demonstration, Self-assessment
Week 4
Visual Arts
Puppetry and Mask Making

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Identify materials used for glove puppetry; b) Construct a functional glove puppet using locally available materials; c) Display creativity in puppet embellishment.
How can recycled materials be transformed into creative puppets?
Learners collect fabric pieces, paper-mâché, and buttons, construct glove puppet bodies, attach head pieces, and decorate them for character roles.
Fabric scraps, papier-mâché, glue, thread, needles, buttons, acrylic paints.
Practical demonstration, Portfolio evaluation, Peer review
Week 5
Sports and Games
Athletics - Field Events (Long Jump)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Describe the four phases of long jump; b) Execute proper single-foot take-off and landing technique; c) Observe safety precautions in the long jump pit.
What role does take-off power play in achieving jump distance?
Learners perform approach runs, practice single-leg take-offs off a board, land safely with bent knees in a prepared sand pit, and measure jump distances.
Sand pit, rake, takeoff board, measuring tape, whistle, marker cones.
Practical performance evaluation, Teacher observation checklist, Oral review
Week 6
Sports and Games
Athletics - Track Events (Relay Races)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Identify non-visual baton exchange techniques; b) Demonstrate baton passing within the changeover zone in a 4x100m relay; c) Show teamwork during relay practice.
Why is timing crucial during a baton exchange in relay races?
Learners work in teams of four to drill non-visual baton passing (upsweep and downsweep methods) within designated changeover zones while running.
Relay batons, running track, marking cones, stopwatches, whistle.
Practical demonstration, Peer observation, Group performance rating
Week 7
Sports and Games
Ball Games - Netball / Basketball Skills

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Differentiate between a chest pass and a bounce pass; b) Execute accurate chest and bounce passes during target drills; c) Demonstrate fair play in small-sided games.
How does choice of pass affect ball speed and tactical advantage in a game?
Learners perform paired passing drills, practice footwork and pivoting techniques, and apply passes in 3v3 mini-game scenarios.
Netballs, basketballs, markings, bibs, whistle, training cones.
Practical assessment, Observation rubric, Oral questioning
Week 8
Sports and Games
Gymnastics (Floor Exercises & Balances)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Execute a forward roll with correct tuck position; b) Perform static partner balances maintaining core stability; c) Adhere to safety guidelines on gymnastics mats.
How does core stability enhance body balance in gymnastics?
Learners warm up core muscles, practice tuck-and-roll movements on mats, work in pairs to form balance pyramids, and provide mutual spotting.
Gymnastics mats, whistle, safety rule charts, video clips.
Practical demonstration, Spotter checklist, Peer feedback
Week 9
Physical Fitness and Health
Fitness Testing (Agility and Flexibility)

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Measure personal flexibility using the sit-and-reach test; b) Perform shuttle runs to measure agility; c) Appreciate personal fitness improvement over time.
Why is physical agility essential in sports and daily activities?
Learners set up test stations, perform sit-and-reach tests, run 10-meter shuttle tests, record results in personal health logs, and compare with standards.
Sit-and-reach box, tape measure, stopwatches, cones, fitness logbooks.
Student fitness logs, Practical performance assessment, Self-evaluation
Week 10
Performing Arts
Play Production & Skit Integration

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Integrate drama, music, and dance into a short skit; b) Rehearse roles using proper vocal expression and movement; c) Appreciate collaborative theater work.
How do integrated arts enhance storytelling in social drama?
Learners form drama groups, script short skits addressing social themes, incorporate background recorder music and dance, and rehearse stage positioning.
Script templates, simple props, musical instruments, stage area.
Practical performance, Portfolio (skit scripts), Peer appraisal
Week 11
Integrated Project
Creative Arts and Sports Exhibition

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Display visual art pieces created during the term; b) Perform a mini music and sports skills exhibition; c) Express pride in personal and group achievements.
How does an exhibition foster community appreciation of arts and sports?
Learners arrange sculpture artifacts and puppets on display tables, present music ensembles and gymnastics routines to an audience, and critique displays.
Display tables, artwork tags, audio speakers, gymnastic mats, sports gear.
Exhibition rubric, Portfolio assessment, Authentic teacher feedback
Week 12
Revision & Portfolio
Portfolio Organization and Skill Review

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Organize practical artworks, music sheets, and sports logs in a portfolio; b) Reflect on strengths and areas for growth across CAS strands; c) Demonstrate orderliness.
Why is reflecting on practical learning experiences important for skill mastery?
Learners compile term artifacts, fill self-reflection rubrics, organize physical and digital portfolios, and review key theoretical concepts across all strands.
Student portfolio binders, assessment rubrics, summary worksheets.
Portfolio evaluation rubric, Oral reflection, Self-assessment
Week 13
Assessment
Term 3 Summative Assessment

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Answer written evaluation questions covering Grade 7 CAS Term 3 strands; b) Demonstrate practical mastery in selected music, art, and sports tasks; c) Exhibit integrity.
How do practical and written assessments evaluate total competency in CAS?
Learners sit for end-of-term written assessment papers and complete individual practical stations for sports skills, instrumental playing, and art evaluation.
Assessment papers, practical scorecards, sports equipment, musical instruments.
Written examination, Standardized practical performance scoring
Week 14
Closure & Evaluation
Term Closure, Reporting, and Equipment Care

By the end of the lesson, the learner should be able to: a) Review term assessment results and constructive feedback; b) Clean, organize, and store sports and art equipment safely; c) Demonstrate responsibility in facility care.
Why is safe storage and maintenance of sports and art materials essential?
Learners receive individual assessment feedback, clean practical rooms, inspect and store musical instruments and sports equipment, and complete term reports.
Report cards, equipment inventory sheets, storage cabinets, cleaning materials.
Inventory checklist, Self-evaluation, Teacher observation
